description: This study assesses how sea-level rise could disrupt Qatar’s road network using geospatial exposure analysis, traffic simulation and graph metrics. It combines projections from IPCC AR6 and NOAA’s 2022 assessment with the Qatar Strategic Transport Model (QSTM), implemented through PTV VISUM. The authors test eight static sea-level-rise scenarios, from 1.61 to 3.31 metres, and compare vehicle-hours travelled, trips and a Network Vulnerability Index. In the most severe scenario, reported vehicle-hours travelled rise by 1,496% over the baseline, while trip durations can increase up to 15 times. Coverage is Qatar, including traffic-congestion patterns in Doha. The 2025 article is available free online in Transportation Research Part D under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: the future sea-level-rise projections are applied to a present-day traffic model as static snapshots, without probability weighting or evolving adaptation. The publisher’s data-availability statement says the authors do not have permission to share the underlying data. The case can inform coastal road-risk and transport-network resilience studies. Resources used include the Qatar Strategic Transport Model, sea-level-rise projections and PTV VISUM (model-ptv-visum), with a link to the existing VISUM model record.
